content.text: Read ONLY docs/submission-design.md, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-12-submission.md and pyproject.toml in this PatchPilot repo. Do not read .env, .data, user configuration, credentials or other files; do not modify files or call network tools. Provide a short review of the planned evidence-led repair product and the Python 3.12 neatlogs compatibility choice, identify one concrete risk and mitigation. This read-only design review will be attached as genuine Entire development evidence. Do not claim you used Entire hooks.
I’ll read the three specified files and give a short review with one concrete risk and mitigation.

The planned product has a clear, bounded value: repair API adapters with a proof linking the contract, version evidence, citations, baseline, diff and independent verification. Separate counterexample auditing strengthens that proof, while keeping additional coverage distinct from user acceptance cases avoids overstating success. These are design commitments; this review does not establish implementation or test results.

Python 3.12 is a reasonable compatibility choice given the design’s stated neatlogs limitation on Python 3.14. Pinning `neatlogs==1.4.26` also improves reproducibility. SDK compatibility was not independently verified here.

One concrete risk: `requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.14"` permits Python 3.13 despite the documented intention to pin 3.12. Mitigate by aligning metadata to `==3.12.*`, making installation select 3.12, and verifying real SDK spans and trace readback on that interpreter.

I read only the three requested files, modified nothing, and made no network calls. I did not use or verify Entire hooks.
